content: Yes, that is correct. In Swiss referendums, each of the 26 cantons is allocated one vote, regardless of its population size. For a proposal to be accepted, it must receive a simple majority of the national vote (i.e., more than 50% of all voters who cast ballots) and a simple majority of the cantons (i.e., more than half of the 26 cantons). This dual-majority requirement is a distinctive feature of Switzerland's direct democracy system.
